title: Forty Doors
logline: In one ordinary day at a small-town temple's lay meditation class, a teacher sends a grieving widow to loving-kindness, a proud young trader to a reflection on the body, and a doubtful engineer to the breath, each to their own plain object.
human_question: If there is one path, why does it start in so many different places?

premise.story: A single day, or a few sessions, at a lay meditation class, following the teacher's quiet, practical matching of different people to different simple practices.
premise.place: A small-town temple hall used for a regular lay meditation class, not a remote forest hermitage.
premise.experience: The variety and ordinariness of what people are actually asked to do: watch a breath, recall a kindness, look at a disc, remember a gift given.

concept_links.why: The source lists forty meditation subjects and insists the choice must fit the person's temperament and be given by a teacher, each with its own reach and limit [C085-M:L3; C085-P:L47].
The kasiṇa disc is one of the forty; a brief glimpse of it being used situates the earlier disc-making idea inside this larger list.
The source separates settling, this class's work, from seeing, the further work of insight, and is clear that settling alone is not the end of the road [C096-P4:L26].

what_camera_could_observe: Several very different people arriving for the same weekly class
Short, separate conversations where the teacher asks about each person's life before suggesting an object
The room settling into silence with everyone doing something different
People leaving, briefly saying what, if anything, they noticed
what_must_be_real: A real, ongoing class with a real teacher and real participants. No practice or conversation is staged for the camera; consent is needed from everyone shown.

possible_arc.opening: The hall filling before the class starts.
possible_arc.turn: The teacher's private, practical matching of person to practice.
possible_arc.ending_open: What each participant says afterwards, in their own words, closes the film.

requirements: A real, regular lay meditation class with a willing teacher
Participants willing to be identified only as much as they choose
A room, not a forest retreat, to keep this distinct from Episode 1's monastery

suggestions.name: A town temple's lay meditation society
suggestions.why: Such weekly classes are common at temples across the island.
suggestions.verify: No specific temple or teacher is identified.

risks: Turning into a lecture about the forty subjects
Exposing private reasons people are grieving or struggling
Implying anyone in the class has attained anything
drop_if: No teacher and class will allow filming without disrupting or exposing participants

connections.note: Both look at the plain, made objects a meditator's attention rests on, from opposite ends: making one object closely, and choosing among forty.
From settling the mind to the further work of seeing clearly, which the next idea follows into ordinary working wisdom.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
